mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates indicate tight monetary conditions, which can lead to decreased corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX shows positive 20-day returns despite high FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1300 signals strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns occur despite HOUST exceeding 1300.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment (UNRATE below 5%) indicates a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns occur with UNRATE below 5%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO above 115) signals economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns occur despite INDPRO exceeding 115.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns occur despite increases in both HOUST and RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, high FEDFUNDS leads to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur during tightening with high FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment (UNRATE) combined with high payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns occur despite low UNRATE and high PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) above 11500 indicates strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns occur despite GDPC1 exceeding 11500.
